remediation_steps.step:
Back up the source file before making any edits.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: OWASP recommends maintaining the ability to rollback any security fix to the pre-fix state in case the change introduces functional regressions.

Edit the source file to replace the vulnerable logging pattern with a secure one that redacts sensitive information.

Command:
  #EDIT_FILE
  {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
   "old_text": "logger.info(\"Received event: [REDACTED]\")",
   "new_text": "logger.info(\"Received event: [REDACTED]\")"}

Why: Redacting sensitive information from logs prevents unauthorized access to sensitive data, aligning with OWASP's secure logging practices.

Verify that the vulnerable logging pattern is no longer present in the source file.

Command:
  #VERIFY_ABSENT
  {"path": "/opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py",
   "pattern": "logger.info(\"Received event: [REDACTED]\")"}

Why: Ensuring the removal of the vulnerable pattern confirms that sensitive data will not be logged.

Perform a syntax check to ensure the edited file is still valid Python code.

Command:
    python3 -m py_compile /opt/vuln-labs/serverless-lab/lambda_function.py

Why: Syntax checking ensures that the code changes did not introduce any syntax errors, maintaining application stability.
